through folded steps (named on the line)
another proof of the same statement

g.title: Parking.log_one_add_taylor — For $u\ge0$ the Taylor polynomials of $\log(1+u)$ bound it alternately: the polynomial of even degree from below and the polynomial of odd degree from above.
Parking.IsRenewal — $u$ is the renewal sequence of the kernel $f$: $u_0=1$ and $u_n=\sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iu_{n-i}$ for every $n\ge1$.
Parking.renewal_logConvex — The renewal sequence of a positive log-convex kernel is log-convex: if $f_i>0$ and $f_{j+2}^2\le f_{j+1}f_{j+3}$, then $u_{n+1}^2\le u_nu_{n+2}$ for all $n$.

Parking.resolvent — If $G$ is the renewal sequence of a kernel $f$ and $v_s=\iota_s+\sum_{i=1}^{s}f_iv_{s-i}$ for all $s$, then $v$ is the convolution of $G$ with $\iota$: $v_s=\sum_{c=0}^{s}G_{s-c}\,\iota_c$.
Parking.abelW — The weights of Abel's binomial identity: $w_0(x) = 1$ and $w_k(x) = x\,(x+k)^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$, for a real number $x$.
Parking.abel_identity — Abel's binomial identity: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, w_k(x)\,(y-k)^{n-k} = (x+y)^n$ for real $x$, $y$, where $w_0(x) = 1$ and $w_k(x) = x\,(x+k)^{k-1}$ for $k \ge 1$.
Parking.cay — The Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ for $j \ge 1$, with $a_0 = 0$.
Parking.cay_conv — The convolution identity of the Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ ($a_0 = 0$): $\sum_{\alpha=1}^{t-1} \alpha\, a_\alpha\, a_{t-\alpha} = (t-1)\, a_t$ for every $t \ge 0$.
Parking.cay_logconvex — The Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ are log-convex on $j \ge 1$, in the cross-multiplied form $a_{u+c}\,a_v \le a_u\,a_{v+c}$ for $1 \le u \le v$ and $c \ge 0$.
Parking.cay_ratio — Consecutive Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ have the ratio $a_{j+1}/a_j = (1 + 1/j)^{j-1}$ for $j \ge 1$.
Parking.cc — The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ for $n \ge 0$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ divided by $n!$. They are the Cayley coefficients shifted by one, $c_n = a_{n+1}$.

Parking.cc_rec — The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ satisfy $(n+1)\,c_{n+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} (j+1)\,c_j\,c_{n-j}$ for every $n \ge 0$: the last-car recursion of parking functions without a displacement bound, divided by $n!$.
Parking.eps — The numbers $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$ (so $\varepsilon_1 = 1$), with $\varepsilon_0 = 0$.
Parking.ren — The sequence $\operatorname{ren}(n) = n^n/n!$ for $n \ge 0$, with $\operatorname{ren}(0) = 1$.

Parking.hasSum_borel — The series $\sum_{j \ge 1} e^{-j} a_j$, with the Cayley coefficients $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$, converges and has the sum $1$: the Borel law with parameter $1$ is a probability law, or, in other words, the tree function takes the value $1$ at its singularity $e^{-1}$.
g.text: total mass of the Borel law

g.title: Parking.hasSum_eps — The series $\sum_{m \ge 1} e^{-m} \varepsilon_m$, with $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$, converges and has the sum $1 - e^{-1}$.
g.text: total mass of the kernel ε at

g.title: Parking.c0 — The constant $c_0 = 1/\sqrt{2\pi} \approx 0.39894$ of Stirling's formula.
Parking.factorial_le_robbins — Robbins' upper bound for the factorial: $n! \le \sqrt{2\pi n}\,(n/e)^n\, e^{1/(12n)}$ for every $n \ge 1$.
Parking.poissonMass — The number $e^{-n} n^n/n!$ for $n \ge 0$: the probability that a Poisson variable with mean $n$ takes the value $n$. Its value at $n = 0$ is $1$.
Parking.poissonMass_ge — The Poisson mass is at least its Stirling approximation times $1 - \frac{1}{12n}$: $(1 - \frac{1}{12n})/\sqrt{2\pi n} \le e^{-n} n^n/n!$ for every $n \ge 1$.
Parking.poissonMass_le — The Poisson mass is at most its Stirling approximation: $e^{-n} n^n/n! \le 1/\sqrt{2\pi n}$ for every $n \ge 1$.
Parking.TreeSeries.Eser — The formal power series $E = 1/P$, the inverse of $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ with $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
Parking.TreeSeries.Pser — The formal power series $P = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$ with real coefficients, where $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
g.text: the series P of the numbers

g.title: Parking.TreeSeries.Tser — The tree series $T = X P = \sum_{j \ge 1} a_j X^j$, a formal power series with real coefficients, where $a_j = j^{j-1}/j!$ are the Cayley coefficients and $P = \sum_n c_n X^n$ with $c_n = a_{n+1}$.

Parking.TreeSeries.coeff_Eser_mul — For every real power series $f$, the coefficients of $f/P$ are $[X^n](E f) = f_n - \sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m f_{n-m}$, where $P = \sum_n c_n X^n$, $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$, $E = 1/P$ and $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$. Equivalently, $1/P = 1 - \sum_{m \ge 1} \varepsilon_m X^m$.
Parking.eps_conv — The numbers $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$ satisfy the renewal equation $c_n = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \varepsilon_m\, c_{n-m}$ for $n \ge 1$, with the kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.
Parking.eps_logconvex — The prime kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ is log-convex: $\varepsilon_{m+1}^2 \le \varepsilon_m\,\varepsilon_{m+2}$ for every $m \ge 1$.

Parking.gs — The step ratio $g_m = \varepsilon_{m+1}/\varepsilon_m$ of the prime kernel $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$, defined by the explicit formula $g_1 = \frac12$, $g_m = \frac{m}{m+1}\bigl(1+\frac1{m-1}\bigr)^{m-1}$ for $m \ge 2$.
g.text: step ratio of the prime kernel

g.title: Parking.extreme_column_le — Let $G$ be the renewal sequence of a positive log-convex kernel $f$, let $v$ have nonnegative innovations with respect to $f$ up to time $\rho$, and let the weights $\theta$ be nonnegative and nondecreasing on $M,\dots,\rho$. Then $\bigl(\sum_{m=M}^{\rho}\theta_mf_mv_{\rho-m}\bigr)G_\rho \le \bigl(\sum_{m=M}^{\rho}\theta_mf_mG_{\rho-m}\bigr)v_\rho$.
Parking.caseFar — Let $k \ge 82$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is positive on the rows $k + r_q \le j < k + r$, where $r_q \le k/3$ and $0.47k < r \le k-1$, then $d_{k+r,k} > 0$.
Parking.chain_column — For $k \ge 2$ and $k + 1 \le n \le 2k-2$: if $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$, then $b(n+1,k-1) < b(n+1,k)$.
g.text: persistence of the sign along a

g.title: Parking.chain_column_iter — For $k \ge 2$ and $k + 1 \le m \le n \le 2k-1$: if $b(m,k-1) < b(m,k)$, then $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$.
g.text: persistence of the sign in the

g.title: Parking.crossing_row — For every $k \ge 82$ there is a row $k + r$ with $1 \le r \le 0.27k$ at which $b(k+r,k-1) < b(k+r,k)$.
g.text: an early positive row in every

g.title: Parking.persist — Let $k \ge 82$ and $1 \le r_q \le k/3$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is nonpositive on the rows $k \le j < k + r_q$ and positive at the row $k + r_q$, then $d_{n,k} > 0$ for every row $k + r_q \le n \le 2k-1$.
Parking.single_crossing — Every column $k \ge 82$ has a row $q$ with $k+1 \le q \le k + 0.27k$ such that $b(j,k) \le b(j,k-1)$ for $k \le j < q$ and $b(n,k-1) < b(n,k)$ for $q \le n \le 2k-1$.
g.text: single crossing of a column k

g.title: Parking.caseA — Let $k \ge 42$. If $d_{j,k} = b(j,k) - b(j,k-1)$ is nonpositive on the rows $k \le j < q$ and positive on the rows $q \le j < n$, where $q = k + r_q$, $n = q + t$, $r_q, t \ge 1$ and $n - k \le 0.47k$, then $d_{n,k} > 0$.

Parking.Fk_anti — For $k \ge 42$ the quantity $(k+\rho)\,\kappa_\rho$, with $\kappa_\rho = \varepsilon_\rho/\gamma_k^\rho$ the tilted kernel at the diagonal tilt, is nonincreasing in $\rho$ on the range $1 \le \rho \le 0.47k$.

Parking.persistence_inequality — An abstract lower bound for a column $\delta$ at a row $n$. From the column equation at $n$, a diagonal lower bound $\gamma u_{j-1} - u_j \le \delta_j$ on the rows $k,\dots,n-1$, a kernel $\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon_{m+1} \le \gamma\varepsilon_m$ for $m < \tau$, and $\delta \ge 0$ on the $\tau - 1$ rows before $n$: $\bigl(\frac2n - \varepsilon_\tau/\gamma^{\tau-1}\bigr)u_{n-1} + \sum_{m=\tau}^{n-k-1}(\gamma\varepsilon_m - \varepsilon_{m+1})\,u_{n-1-m} \le \delta_n$.
Parking.Gres — The sequence $G_s = e^{-s}\sum_{j=0}^{s}2^{-j}\,[X^s]\,X^jP^{j+1}$, where $P = \sum_n c_nX^n$ and $c_n = (n+1)^{n-1}/n!$. It is the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel.
Parking.Gres_isRenewal — The sequence $G$ is the renewal sequence of the frozen kernel $f$: $G_0 = 1$ and $G_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n}f_iG_{n-i}$ for $n \ge 1$.
Parking.Gres_lower — For $s \ge 6$ the resolvent sequence of the frozen kernel satisfies $G_s \ge e\,\bigl(1-\frac1{12(s+1)}\bigr)\bigl(4-\frac{21}{s+1}\bigr)\big/\bigl((s+1)\sqrt{2\pi(s+1)}\bigr)$.
Parking.Gres_sum_le — Every partial sum of the resolvent sequence of the frozen kernel is at most $2e$: $\sum_{s<N}G_s \le 2e$.

Parking.fker — The frozen kernel $f$: $f_1 = \frac32 e^{-1}$ and $f_i = e^{-i}\varepsilon_i$ for $i \ge 2$, where $\varepsilon_i = (i-1)^{i-1}/i!$. It is the prime kernel in the Borel scale with $\frac12e^{-1}$ added at the index $1$.

Parking.two_point — An abstract persistence statement. A sequence $\eta$ satisfies a column equation with feedback kernel $\kappa$ at a crossing row $q$ and at a later row $n$, is bounded below by the decrements of a nonnegative profile $U$ in between, is nonpositive before $q$ and positive on $[q, n)$; if $\kappa$ is positive, nonincreasing and log-convex in cross form and satisfies a condition comparing the two rows, then $\eta_n > 0$.

Parking.bq_L0 — The column equation of the level $l\ge1$ on the rows $l+1\le n\le 2l+1$: $\beta^{(l)}_n=\frac1n z^{(l+1)}_{n-1}+\frac ln\beta^{(l)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-l-1}\varepsilon_m\beta^{(l)}_{n-m}$, where $\beta^{(l)}_n=b(n,l)/n!$.
Parking.dq — The normalised step of the column $k$ in the row $n$: $\delta^{(k)}_n=\beta^{(k)}_n-\beta^{(k-1)}_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$.
Parking.dq_base — The first nonzero value of the step of the column $k\ge2$: $\delta^{(k)}_k=-a_k/k$ with $a_k=k^{k-1}/k!$; in integers, $b(k,k)-b(k,k-1)=-k^{k-2}$.
g.text: initial value of the step of a

g.title: Parking.dq_col — The column equation of the step of the column $k\ge2$ on the rows $k+1\le n\le 2k-1$: $\delta_n=\frac{k+1}{n}\delta_{n-1}+\frac2n\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1}+\sum_{m=1}^{n-k}\varepsilon_m\delta_{n-m}$, where $\delta_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$.
Parking.gam — The factor $\gamma_k=(1+1/k)^{k-2}$ of the diagonal lower bound $\gamma_k\,\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1}\le\beta^{(k)}_n$.
Parking.xi — The tree curvature coefficients $\xi_t$ of the column $k$: $\xi_0=0$ and, for $t\ge1$, $t\,\xi_t=\min(t,k+1)\,z^{(k+1)}_{t-1}-2\min(t,k)\,z^{(k)}_{t-1}+\min(t,k-1)\,z^{(k-1)}_{t-1}$.

Parking.zr_diag_mono — Stochastic monotonicity along the diagonal: for $y\ge1$ and every $n$, $z^{(y)}_n/c_n\le z^{(y+1)}_{n+1}/c_{n+1}$; that is, the probability that a uniform parking function of length $n$ has maximum displacement below $y$ does not decrease when $n$ and $y$ are both raised by one.

Parking.A_succ — The last-car recursion: the number $A(n+1,k)$ of parking functions of length $n+1$ with maximum displacement at most $k$ equals $\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,k+1)\binom nj A(j,k)\,A(n-j,k)$.
Parking.d_eq_A — For $k\ge2$ the step $b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)$ of the column $k$ in the row $n$ is the second difference $A(n,k)-2A(n,k-1)+A(n,k-2)$ of the cumulative counts in the bound $k$.

Parking.IsWSol — The predicate "$W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with weight $\omega$": $W_0=1$ and $(n+1)W_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\omega(j+1)\,W_j\,W_{n-j}$ for all $n\ge0$, for real sequences $\omega$ and $W$.

Parking.IsWSol.ez — Single-chain formula, quotient form. If $W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with a weight that satisfies $\omega(t)=t$ for $1\le t\le k$, then for $1\le n\le 2k+1$ the quantity $W_n-\sum_{m=1}^{n}\varepsilon_mW_{n-m}$ is $0$ for $n\le k$ and $\frac{\omega(n)}{n}W_{n-1}-c_{n-1}$ for $n>k$.

Parking.IsWSol.fwd — Single-chain formula, forward form. If $W$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with a weight that satisfies $\omega(t)=t$ for $1\le t\le k$, then for $n\le 2k+1$: $c_n-W_n=\sum_{t=k+1}^{n}c_{n-t}\bigl(c_{t-1}-\frac{\omega(t)}{t}W_{t-1}\bigr)$.
Parking.bq — The normalised count $\beta^{(k)}_n=b(n,k)/n!$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $k$, divided by $n!$.
Parking.zr — The normalised cumulative count $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$: the number of parking functions of length $n$ all of whose displacements are smaller than the threshold $y$, divided by $n!$.
Parking.zr_eq_cc — In the free range $n\le y$ of a threshold $y\ge1$ the normalised cumulative count equals the Cayley number: $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!=c_n=(n+1)^{n-1}/n!$.
g.text: the free range of a threshold

g.title: Parking.zr_isWSol — For a threshold $y\ge1$ the sequence $z^{(y)}_n=A(n,y-1)/n!$ solves the weighted last-car recursion with the weight $\omega(t)=\min(t,y)$: $z^{(y)}_0=1$ and $(n+1)z^{(y)}_{n+1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\min(j+1,y)\,z^{(y)}_jz^{(y)}_{n-j}$.

Parking.cross_of_bounds — The crossing criterion with its five sums replaced by closed-form bounds: for $k\ge2$ and $2\le R\le k-1$, three explicit inequalities between elementary functions of $k$ and $R$ imply that $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$ in some row $j$ with $k<j\le k+R$.

Parking.SR — The sum $S_R=\sum_{i=0}^{R-1}(ix)^i/i!$ for the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$; $x\,S_R$ is the first moment $\sum_{m=1}^{R}m\,\kappa_m$ of the tilted kernel masses up to $R$.

Parking.Somg — The sum $\Sigma_\omega=\sum_{i=k+1}^{N-1}(i-k+1)\,\omega_i$, $N=k+R$, of the flow factors $\omega_i=1-i/((i+1)x\gamma_i)$ of the column $k$, each weighted by its distance from the row $k$ plus one.

Parking.cross_criterion — The crossing criterion: for a column $k\ge2$ and $1\le R\le k-1$, two explicit inequalities in $k$ and $R$ (the kernel deficit $\bar\kappa_R$ is nonnegative, and a product of two explicit sums is smaller than a third) imply that $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$ in some row $j$ with $k<j\le k+R$.

Parking.ecor — The correction $\mathsf e_j=(j-k+2)-\Pi_{j+1}/\pi_{j+1}$ of the column $k$: the amount by which the sum $\Pi_{j+1}=\pi_k+\dots+\pi_{j+1}$ of the weights, divided by its last term, falls short of its number of terms.
Parking.ecorSum — The sum $\mathsf E=\sum_{j=k}^{N-2}\mathsf e_j/(j+1)$, $N=k+R$, of the tilt corrections $\mathsf e_j$ of the column $k$ over the rows below the last two.
Parking.kapx — The tilted kernel masses $\kappa_m=x^m\varepsilon_m$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt of the column and $\varepsilon_m=(m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.
Parking.kbar — The kernel deficit $\bar\kappa_M=1-x-\sum_{m=1}^{M}\kappa_m$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt and $\kappa_m=x^m\varepsilon_m$ are the tilted kernel masses.

Parking.omg — The factor $\omega_i=1-i/((i+1)\,x\gamma_i)$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt and $\gamma_i=(1+1/i)^{i-2}$; it bounds the diagonal increase of the cumulative proportion in the row $i$.
Parking.pix — The weights $\pi_j=x^ja_j/j$ of the column $k$, where $x=1/\gamma_k$ is the diagonal tilt of the column and $a_j=j^{j-1}/j!$.
Parking.pixSum — The partial sums $\Pi_i=\sum_{n=k}^{i}\pi_n$ of the weights $\pi_n=x^na_n/n$ of the column $k$, starting at the index $k$.

Parking.profD — The tilted profile $u_j=x^j\,\beta^{(k-1)}_j$ of the column $k$: the normalised counts $b(j,k-1)/j!$ of the column $k-1$, multiplied by the powers of the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$.
Parking.stepD — The tilted step $\eta_n=x^n\,\delta_n$ of the column $k$: the normalised step $\delta_n=(b(n,k)-b(n,k-1))/n!$ multiplied by the powers of the diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$.
g.text: tilted step at the diagonal tilt

g.title: Parking.xk — The diagonal tilt $x=1/\gamma_k$ of the column $k$, where $\gamma_k=(1+1/k)^{k-2}$; for $k\ge2$ it is $x=(k/(k+1))^{k-2}$.
Parking.crossing_strip — Every column $k\ge265$ is positive in some row $j>k$ with $25\,(j-k-1)^3\le121\,k^2$: there is a row $j$ with $k<j\le k+\lfloor(11k/5)^{2/3}\rfloor+1$ and $b(j,k)>b(j,k-1)$.
Parking.A — $A(n,k)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is at most $k$, that is, in which every car parks at most $k$ spots after the spot it prefers.
Parking.b — $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is exactly $\ell$.
Parking.dispList — The displacements of the cars: for a sequence of preferences $(a_1,\dots,a_m)$ and the sequence $(p_1,\dots,p_m)$ of the spots taken, the sequence of the differences $p_i-a_i$.

Parking.firstFree — The spot taken by a car with preference $a$ on a street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$ when the spots of a set $U$ are occupied: the least spot $s\ge a$ of the street that is not in $U$, and no spot at all if there is none.
g.text: first free spot at or after a

g.title: Parking.maxDisp — The maximum displacement $M(\alpha)$ of a parking function $\alpha$: the largest difference between the spot a car takes and the spot it prefers. It is undefined when $\alpha$ is not a parking function.

Parking.parkFrom — The parking process: cars with given preferences arrive one after another at a street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$, some of them already occupied, and each takes the first free spot at or after its preference. The result is the sequence of the spots taken, and it is undefined if some car cannot park.
Parking.positions — The spots taken by the $n$ cars of a preference sequence $\alpha$ when they arrive in order at an empty street with the spots $0,\dots,n-1$; undefined if some car cannot park.
Parking.prefList — The preferences of a function $\alpha$ from $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ to itself, written as the sequence $(\alpha(0),\dots,\alpha(n-1))$ of natural numbers.

Parking.big_columns — For every column $k\ge 82$ and every row $n\ge 2k$: $b(n,k-1)<b(n,k)$, where $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$.

Parking.FirstLayer.conv_TK — If a positive sequence $f$ satisfies the tilted convexity $2e^{\mu/k}f(j+1)\le e^{\mu}f(j+2)+e^{-\mu}f(j)$ for $j\le n$ and all $\mu\ge 0$, has $f(n+2)=f(n+1)\le f(a)$ for $a\le n$, and $n+2\le k$, then its self-convolutions at the lengths $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$ have property K at $k$.

Parking.FirstLayer.Sdir_TK — For $k\ge 7$ and $1\le\rho\le k-2$, the values $S_\rho(k-1)$, $S_\rho(k)$, $S_\rho(k+1)$ of the direct term of the first-layer recursion at the critical tilt $x_k$ form a triple with property K at $k$.
g.text: property K of the direct term

g.title: Parking.FirstLayer.kernel_TK — For $k\ge 7$ and $0\le\rho\le k-2$, at the critical tilt $x_k$, the tilted masses $u^{(k-1)}_{k-1+\rho}$, $u^{(k)}_{k+\rho}$, $u^{(k+1)}_{k+1+\rho}$ of the thresholds $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ at the sizes that exceed the threshold by $\rho$ form a triple with property K at $k$.
g.text: triples of tilted masses in the

g.title: Parking.FirstLayer.zrT_diag_convex — For $k\ge 7$ and $k\le N\le 2k-2$, at the critical tilt $x_k$: $u^{(k+1)}_{N+1}-2u^{(k)}_N+u^{(k-1)}_{N-1}\ge 0$, where $u^{(y)}_M=z^{(y)}_Mx_k^{\,M}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $y$.
g.text: tilted masses in the first layer

g.title: Parking.FirstLayer.zrT_weak_requirement — For $k\ge 7$, $k\le N\le 2k-2$ and every real $c\ge k$, at the critical tilt $x_k$: $(c+1)\,u^{(k+1)}_{N+1}-2c\,u^{(k)}_N+(c-1)\,u^{(k-1)}_{N-1}\ge 0$, where $u^{(y)}_M=z^{(y)}_Mx_k^{\,M}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $y$.
g.text: in the first layer, for every

g.title: Parking.FirstLayer.TK_ccT_top — At the critical tilt of a column $k\ge 3$, the triple $(\omega_{k-1},\omega_k,\omega_{k+1})$ of tilted Cayley masses $\omega_n=c_nx_k^{\,n}$ has property K at $k$.

Parking.FirstLayer.ccT_tilt_mid — At the critical tilt of a column $k\ge 3$, the tilted Cayley masses $\omega_n=c_nx_k^n$ satisfy $2e^{\mu/k}\omega_{j+1}\le e^{\mu}\omega_{j+2}+e^{-\mu}\omega_j$ for every $j$ with $j+2\le k$ and every real $\mu$.

Parking.FirstLayer.pairT_TK — For $k\ge 3$ and $\rho+n+2=k$, the pair sums $Q_\rho(n)$, $Q_\rho(n+1)$, $Q_\rho(n+2)$ of tilted Cayley masses at the critical tilt $x_k$ form a triple with property K at $k$.
g.text: property K of the pair sums

g.title: Parking.FirstLayer.TK — Property K at $k$ of a triple of real numbers $(a,b,c)$: the inequality $2e^{\mu/k}b\le e^{\mu}c+e^{-\mu}a$ holds for every real $\mu\ge 0$.

Parking.FirstLayer.TK.mul_prod — Property K at $k>1$ is preserved when the three values are multiplied by the values at $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ of $z\mapsto(z+a)(z+b)/z$, where $a,b\ge 0$ and $ab\le k^2-1$, provided the middle value is nonnegative.

Parking.FirstLayer.TK.mul_ratio — Property K at $k>1$ is preserved when the three values are multiplied by the values at $k-1$, $k$, $k+1$ of $z\mapsto(z+\alpha)/(z+\beta)$, $0\le\alpha\le\beta$, provided the middle value is nonnegative.

Parking.FirstLayer.direct — The direct part $D(c,P)=\sum_{a=0}^{c-P}\min(P+a+1,c)\,\omega_{P+a}\,\omega_{c-a}$ of the last-car recursion at the size $c+P+1$ and the threshold $c$: the terms in which both pieces have size at most $c$.

Parking.FirstLayer.zrT_split — For a threshold $c\ge 1$ and $P\le c$, at the tilt $x_k$: $(c+P+1)\,u^{(c)}_{c+P+1}=x_k\big(\sum_{i<P}(c+i+1)\,\omega_i\,u^{(c)}_{c+P-i}+D(c,P)\big)$, where $u^{(c)}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $c$, $\omega$ the tilted Cayley masses and $D(c,P)$ the direct part.

Parking.order_neg — For a column $k\ge 2$, a row $q\le k+\frac{27}{100}k$, a row $n\ge 2k$ and every $j<q$: $\kappa_{n-j}\,(2k-1)\le\kappa_{n-q+1}\,\Psi'(j)$, where $\kappa$ is the prime kernel of the threshold $k$ at the critical tilt and $\Psi'(j)=\max(j,2k-1)$.
g.text: order of the kernel weights on

g.title: Parking.order_pos — For a column $k\ge 2$, a row $q$ with $k+1\le q\le k+\frac{27}{100}k$, a row $n\ge 2k$ and every $j$ with $q\le j\le n-1$: $\kappa_{n-q+1}\,\Psi'(j)\le\kappa_{n-j}\,(2k-1)$, where $\kappa$ is the prime kernel of the threshold $k$ at the critical tilt and $\Psi'(j)=\max(j,2k-1)$.
g.text: order of the kernel weights on
the rows from the crossing on

g.title: Parking.column_one — For every $n\ge 3$: $b(n,0)\le b(n,1)$, where $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$.
Parking.left_half — For $n\ge 17$ and $k\ge 1$ with $2k\le n$: $b(n,k-1)\le b(n,k)$, where $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$.
g.text: the left half of a row n ≥ 17 is

g.title: Parking.small_columns — For $2\le k\le 81$ and every $n$ with $n\ge 2k$ and $n\ge 17$: $b(n,k-1)\le b(n,k)$, where $b(n,\ell)$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ with maximum displacement exactly $\ell$.

Parking.propagate — Let $k\ge 2$, $n_0\ge k$ and $x>0$. If $z^{(k)}_Nx^N$ does not increase in $N$ and the sums $\sum_{t=s}^{n_0}\xi_t\,x^t$ are nonnegative for all $k\le s\le n_0$, where $\xi_t$ is the tree curvature of column $k$, then the step of column $k$ is nonnegative in every row $n\ge n_0$: $b(n,k-1)\le b(n,k)$.

Parking.DeltaId_nonneg — For $k\ge 7$ and every size $N\ge 2k-1$, at the critical tilt $x_k$: $(N+1)\,u^{(k+1)}_{N+1}-2N\,u^{(k)}_N+(N-1)\,u^{(k-1)}_{N-1}\ge 0$, where $u^{(y)}_M=z^{(y)}_Mx_k^{\,M}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $y$.

Parking.DeltaPsi_nonneg — For $k\ge 7$ and every size $N\ge k$, at the critical tilt $x_k$: $\Psi'(N+1)\,u^{(k+1)}_{N+1}-2\Psi'(N)\,u^{(k)}_N+\Psi'(N-1)\,u^{(k-1)}_{N-1}\ge 0$, where $\Psi'(M)=\max(M,2k-1)$ and $u^{(y)}_M=z^{(y)}_Mx_k^{\,M}$ is the tilted environment of the threshold $y$.
g.text: with the weight Ψ′ on all

g.title: Parking.PsiW — The weight $\Psi'(N)=\max(N,\,2k-1)$ given to the row (or size) $N$ in the argument for a column $k$: constant $2k-1$ up to the row $2k-1$, and equal to $N$ afterwards.
g.text: 2k−1) of the rows of column k

g.title: Parking.Ut_diag_lower — For $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 1$, at the critical tilt $x_k$: $k\,U_{n-1}\le(k+1)\,U^{+}_n$, where $U_N=x_k^{\,N}\,b(N,k-1)/N!$ and $U^{+}_N=x_k^{\,N}\,b(N,k)/N!$ are the tilted masses of the levels $k-1$ and $k$.

Parking.weighted_debt — For $k\ge 7$ and $J\ge k$, at the critical tilt $x_k$, the weighted sum of the tilted steps of column $k$ over the rows $k,\dots,J$ is bounded below by boundary terms: $\sum_{n=k}^{J}\Psi'(n)\,\eta_n\ge-\big(\Psi'(J)U_J+\Psi'(J-1)U_{J-1}+(\Psi'(J)-\Psi'(J-1))\,u^{(k)}_J\big)$.
g.text: the weighted debt of a column

g.title: Parking.Tq_eq — The compositions of $m$ with exactly $q \ge 1$ parts, each part of size $p$ weighted by $a_p = p^{p-1}/p!$, have the total weight $T_{m,q} = a_m\, q\, P_{m,q}$, where $P_{m,q} = \prod_{i<q}(1 - i/m)$ is the birthday tail.
g.text: the birthday law of the number

g.title: Parking.mu0_le_muh — For $r \ge 1$ and $0 < h \le 1$, the mean number of cuts $\mu_r(h)$ of the compositions of $r$ with constant cut weight $h$ is at least $\mu^0_r(X) = \bigl(\sqrt{(4+X)^2 + 12(r-1)} - (4+X)\bigr)/3$ with $X = r(1/h - 1)$.

Parking.tau_succ_le — Shortening by one: for $r \ge 1$ and $0 < h \le 1$, the total weights of the compositions of $r+1$ and of $r$ with constant cut weight $h$ satisfy $\tau_{r+1}(h) \le (1+\frac1r)^r\bigl(1 - \frac{1-h}{2h(r+1)}\,\mu_r(h)\bigr)\,\tau_r(h)$, where $\mu_r(h)$ is the mean number of cuts.

Parking.Dbirth — The number $D_m = \dfrac{3((m+2)s_m - 3m)}{2(m - s_m)}$ formed from the mean $s_m$ of the birthday law of $m$; for $m \ge 2$ it is the ratio of the third to the second factorial moment of that law.
Parking.Pb — The birthday tail $P_{m,j} = \prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(1 - i/m)$: the probability that $j$ independent uniform draws from $m$ values are pairwise distinct.

Parking.sbirth — The number $s_m = \sum_{j=1}^{m} P_{m,j}$, where $P_{m,j} = \prod_{i<j}(1 - i/m)$: the mean of the birthday law of $m$, that is the expected number of uniform draws from $m$ values before the first repetition.

Parking.Gfun — The criterion function $\mathsf{G}(r,k)$: an explicit function of the column $k$ and of the distance $r = n - k$ of a row from it, whose nonnegativity implies that a nonpositive step of column $k$ in the row $n$ forces a negative step of column $k+1$ in the same row.
Parking.Lam — $\Lambda_m[f]$ is the total weight of all compositions of $m$ for the cut profile $f$: the sum over $q$ of the weights $V_q(m;f)$ of the compositions with exactly $q$ parts.
Parking.Tq — $T_{m,q}$ is the total weight of the compositions of $m$ with exactly $q$ parts when each part of size $p$ weighs $a_p = p^{p-1}/p!$ and every cut weighs $1$.

Parking.Vc — For a real function $f$ on the natural numbers (a cut profile), $V_q(m;f)$ is the total weight of the compositions of $m$ with exactly $q$ parts, where a part of size $p$ weighs $a_p = p^{p-1}/p!$ and a cut at the position $s$ weighs $f(s)$.
g.text: with a given number of parts

g.title: Parking.mu0 — $\mu^0_r(X) = \bigl(\sqrt{(4+X)^2 + 12(r-1)} - (4+X)\bigr)/3$, the explicit function that bounds from below the mean number of cuts of a composition of $r$ under a homogeneous law.

Parking.muh — $\mu_r(h)$ is the mean number of cuts of a composition of $r$ under the homogeneous law with parameter $h$, in which a composition with $q$ parts has probability proportional to its Cayley weight times $h^{q-1}$.

Parking.tau — $\tau_m(h)$ is the total weight of the compositions of $m$ when each part of size $p$ weighs $a_p = p^{p-1}/p!$ and every cut weighs the same real number $h$; it equals $\sum_q T_{m,q} h^{q-1}$.

Parking.step_neg_of_Gfun — At a first-layer position $n = k + r$, $2 \le r \le k - 1$, at which the criterion function satisfies $\mathsf{G}(r,k) \ge 0$: if the step of column $k$ in the row $n$ is nonpositive, then the step of column $k + 1$ in the row $n$ is negative.

Parking.curv_ratio — At a position $n = k + r$ with $r \le k - 1$, the second difference of the frozen polynomial $K_{n,k}$ at $k+1$ is at most $e^{D_r/(k-1)}$ times its second difference at $k$, where $D_r$ is the ratio of the third to the second factorial moment of the birthday law on the compositions of $r$.

Parking.Tq_ratio — For the compositions of $m$ in which a part of size $p$ weighs $a_p=p^{p-1}/p!$ and the cuts contribute no factor, the total weights $T_{m,q}$ and $T_{m,q+1}$ of the compositions with $q$ and with $q+1$ parts satisfy $q\,m\,T_{m,q+1}=(q+1)(m-q)\,T_{m,q}$ for every $q\ge1$.

Parking.Vc_ratio_le — If every cut of a composition of $m$ carries a factor between $0$ and $1$, the total weights $V_q$ and $V_{q+1}$ of the compositions with $q$ and with $q+1$ parts satisfy $q\,m\,V_{q+1}\le(q+1)(m-q)\,V_q$ for every $q\ge1$: the ratio $V_{q+1}/V_q$ is at most its value when every cut has the factor $1$.

Parking.Vc_thr_ratio_ge — For the cut profile $s\mapsto1/(N-s)$ with $N>m$, the total weights $V_q$ and $V_{q+1}$ of the compositions of $m$ with $q$ and with $q+1$ parts satisfy $(q+1)(m-q)\,V_q\le q\,m\,(N-\tfrac m2)\,V_{q+1}$ for every $q\ge1$: the ratio $V_{q+1}/V_q$ is at least its value for the constant profile equal to the threshold profile at the midpoint $m/2$.

Parking.Lam_first_cell — Removing the first unit cell of a composition of $r+1$: with $N = k + r + 1$ and $h = (k-1)/(k+r)$, the chain sums satisfy $\Lambda_{r+1}(k-1;N)\,\tau_r(h) \le \tau_{r+1}(h)\,\Lambda_r(k;N)$, so the ratio of the chain sums of the lengths $r+1$ and $r$ is at most the ratio of the totals of the homogeneous model.
g.text: removal of the first unit cell

g.title: Parking.Lam_shorten — With $N = k + r + 1$ and $\mu_-$ the mean number of cuts under the homogeneous law with parameter $(k-1)/(k+r)$ on the compositions of $r$, the chain sums satisfy $\Lambda_{r+1}(k-1;N) \le (1+1/r)^r\,\bigl(1 - \mu_-/(2(k-1))\bigr)\,\Lambda_r(k;N)$.
g.text: shortening a chain sum by one

g.title: Parking.Kpoly — The frozen polynomial $K_{n,k}(y)$ of the position $(n,k)$: a polynomial in the threshold $y$, defined as a combination of chain sums, whose values at $y = k$ and $y = k+1$ are the normalised numbers of parking functions of length $n \le 2k+1$ with all displacements less than $k$ and less than $k+1$.

Parking.dq_frozen — At a first-layer position $n = k + r$, $1 \le r \le k-1$, the normalised steps of the columns $k$ and $k+1$ in the row $n$ are each a second difference of the frozen polynomial $K_{n,k}$ minus a multiple of a chain sum: $d_{n,k}/n! = C_- - B_-$ and $d_{n,k+1}/n! = C_+ - B_+$.

Parking.mono265 — For $k \ge 265$ and $n \ge k + 2$: if column $k$ has no positive step in the rows $k+1, \dots, n$, that is, $b(j,k) \le b(j,k-1)$ for $k + 1 \le j \le n$, then column $k + 1$ has a negative step in the row $n$: $b(n,k+1) < b(n,k)$.

Parking.mono — For $k \ge 9$ and $n \ge k + 2$: if column $k$ has no positive step in the rows $k+1, \dots, n$, that is, $b(j,k) \le b(j,k-1)$ for $k + 1 \le j \le n$, then column $k + 1$ has no positive step in the row $n$: $b(n,k+1) \le b(n,k)$.

Parking.Lam_raise — With $N = k + r + 1$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}$ the mean number of cuts under the homogeneous law with parameter $k/(k+1+r/2)$ on the compositions of $r$, raising the threshold of the chain sum from $k$ to $k+2$ multiplies it by at least $(1+2/k)^{\mu_{\mathrm{mid}}}$.

Parking.sbirth_le — The mean $s_r=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\prod_{i<j}(1-\frac ir)$ of the birthday law with $r$ boxes (Ramanujan's function $Q(r)$) satisfies $s_r\le\sqrt{\pi r/2}\;e^{1/(12r)}-\frac13$ for every $r\ge1$.
g.text: upper bound for the mean of

g.title: Parking.Gfun_pos — The criterion function $\mathsf G(r,k)$ is positive for all integers $k\ge265$ and $r\ge2$ with $25r^3\le121k^2$.

Parking.root_unimodal — The root proposition: for every integer $n\ge1$ the sequence $(b_{n,0},b_{n,1},\dots,b_{n,n-1})$ is unimodal, where $b_{n,\ell}$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is exactly $\ell$.
g.text: root · statement · no proof · settled · formal

g.title: Parking.root_unimodal_proof — The proved main theorem: for every integer $n\ge1$ the sequence $(b_{n,0},b_{n,1},\dots,b_{n,n-1})$ is unimodal, where $b_{n,\ell}$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ whose maximum displacement is exactly $\ell$.

Parking.bq_diag_lower — For $k \ge 2$ and every row $n \ge 1$: $\gamma_k\, \beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1} \le \beta^{(k)}_n$, where $\beta^{(\ell)}_n = b(n,\ell)/n!$ and $\gamma_k = (1+1/k)^{k-2}$. In terms of the counts, $\gamma_k \cdot n \cdot b(n-1,k-1) \le b(n,k)$.

Parking.col_eq_all — For a column $k \ge 2$ and every row $n \ge k+1$: $(k+1)\,\delta_{n-1} + 2\,\beta^{(k-1)}_{n-1} \le n\,\bigl(\delta_n - \sum_{m=1}^{n-k} \kappa^{(k)}_m\, \delta_{n-m}\bigr)$, where $\delta_n = (b(n,k) - b(n,k-1))/n!$ is the normalised step of the column, $\beta^{(k-1)}_n = b(n,k-1)/n!$, and $\kappa^{(k)}$ is the prime kernel of the threshold $k$.

Parking.one_tree_bound — For a column $k \ge 2$ and every row $n$: $\sum_{t=0}^{n} \xi_t\, z^{(k)}_{n-t} \le \delta_n$, where $\xi_t$ is the tree curvature of the column $k$, $z^{(k)}_n = A(n,k-1)/n!$ is the environment of the threshold $k$, and $\delta_n = (b(n,k) - b(n,k-1))/n!$ is the normalised step of the column.

Parking.Gp — The series $\Gamma_y'$ of a threshold $y$: the formal derivative of $\Gamma_y = \sum_{t \ge 1} \frac{\min(t,y)}{t}\, z^{(y)}_{t-1} X^t$, with coefficients $[X^j]\,\Gamma_y' = \min(j+1,y)\, z^{(y)}_j$. It satisfies $Z_y' = \Gamma_y' Z_y$.
Parking.Ks — The prime kernel series $K_y = 1 - 1/Z_y$ of a threshold $y$, where $Z_y$ is the series of the threshold $y$ (`Parking.Zs`).

Parking.Zs — The formal power series $Z_y = \sum_{n \ge 0} z^{(y)}_n X^n$ of a threshold $y$, where $z^{(y)}_n = A(n,y-1)/n!$ is the number of parking functions of length $n$ all of whose displacements are smaller than $y$, divided by $n!$.
Parking.deriv_Ks — For a threshold $y \ge 1$ the prime kernel series $K_y = 1 - 1/Z_y$ satisfies $K_y' = (1 - K_y)\,\Gamma_y'$, where $\Gamma_y' = Z_y'/Z_y$.

Parking.deriv_Zs — For a threshold $y \ge 1$ the series $Z_y$ of the threshold satisfies $Z_y' = \Gamma_y' Z_y$, where $\Gamma_y'$ has the coefficients $\min(j+1,y)\, z^{(y)}_j$. This is the last-car recursion written for power series.
Parking.kq — The prime kernel $\kappa^{(y)}_m$ of a threshold $y$: the coefficient of $X^m$ in the prime kernel series $K_y = 1 - 1/Z_y$.
Parking.kq_eq_eps — In the free range $1 \le m \le y$ the prime kernel of the threshold $y$ is the free prime kernel: $\kappa^{(y)}_m = \varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$.
g.text: the prime kernel in the free

g.title: Parking.kq_rec — For $N \ge y \ge 2$ the prime kernel of the threshold $y$ satisfies $N\,\kappa^{(y)}_N = \sum_{\gamma=1}^{y-1} (y-\gamma)\, a_\gamma\, \kappa^{(y)}_{N-\gamma}$, with $a_\gamma = \gamma^{\gamma-1}/\gamma!$.

Parking.Tab.n0 — For $2\le k\le81$, $n_0(k)$ is the listed row below which the table computes the column $k$, at which it checks the suffix sums of the propagation theorem, and from which on that theorem takes over; it is given by a list of eighty numbers and satisfies $2k+3\le n_0(k)\le2k+14$.
g.text: the row at which a column k

g.title: Parking.Tab.small_table — The computed facts about each column $2\le k\le81$ of the numbers $b(n,k)$: a positive step $b(n,k)-b(n,k-1)$ in a row $k+1\le n\le2k-2$ is followed by a positive step in the row $n+1$, the step is nonnegative in the rows $\max(2k,17)\le n<n_0(k)$, and at the row $n_0(k)$ all the sums $\sum_{t=s}^{n_0(k)}\xi_tx_k^t$, $k\le s\le n_0(k)$, are nonnegative.
g.text: the table of the columns 2 to

g.title: Parking.Tab.small_rows — The computed fact about the rows $n\le16$ of the numbers $b(n,\ell)$: none of them has a strict descent followed by a strict ascent.
g.text: the table of the rows up to 16

g.title: Parking.Tab.two_signs — The two computed signs of each column $9\le k\le264$: with the listed number $z=z(k)$, which satisfies $z+2\le k$, the column $k$ is positive in the row $k+z+1$, $b(k+z+1,k-1)<b(k+z+1,k)$, and the column $k+1$ is negative in the row $k+z$, $b(k+z,k+1)<b(k+z,k)$.
g.text: the table of two signs for the

g.title: Parking.Tab.ztab — For $9\le k\le264$, $z(k)$ is the listed number for which the table of two signs shows that the column $k$ is positive in the row $k+z(k)+1$ and the column $k+1$ is negative in the row $k+z(k)$; it grows from $z(9)=7$ to $z(264)=35$.
g.text: positive row of a column k

g.title: Parking.Ut — The tilted cell $U_N = z^{(k)}_N x^N - z^{(k-1)}_N x^N$ of a column $k$ at a tilt $x$: the difference of the tilted environments of the thresholds $k$ and $k-1$, equal to $b(N,k-1)\,x^N/N!$ for $k \ge 2$.
Parking.cayT — The tilted tree numbers $a_n x^n$ at a tilt $x$, where $a_n = n^{n-1}/n!$ for $n \ge 1$ and $a_0 = 0$.
Parking.ccT — The tilted Cayley masses $c_N x^N$ at a tilt $x$, where $c_N = (N+1)^{N-1}/N!$ is the number of parking functions of length $N$ divided by $N!$.
Parking.epsT — The tilted free prime kernel $\varepsilon_m x^m$ at a tilt $x$, where $\varepsilon_m = (m-1)^{m-1}/m!$ for $m \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon_0 = 0$.
Parking.kqT — The tilted prime kernel $\kappa^{(y)}_m x^m$ of a threshold $y$ at a tilt $x$, where $\kappa^{(y)}_m$ is the coefficient of $X^m$ in $1 - 1/Z_y$.

Parking.kqT_harmonic — Let $y \ge 2$ and $x \ge 0$. If the tilted free prime kernel $\varepsilon_m x^m$ does not increase on $1 \le m \le y$, then the tilted prime kernel $q_m = \kappa^{(y)}_m x^m$ satisfies $(m+1)\,q_{m+1} \le m\,q_m$ for every $m \ge y$.

Parking.kqT_nonneg — For a threshold $y \ge 2$ and a tilt $x \ge 0$ the tilted prime kernel is nonnegative: $\kappa^{(y)}_m x^m \ge 0$ for every $m$. With $x = 1$ this is the nonnegativity of the prime kernel itself.

Parking.kqT_succ_le — Let $y \ge 2$ and $x \ge 0$. If the tilted free prime kernel $\varepsilon_m x^m$ does not increase on $1 \le m \le y$, then the tilted prime kernel $q_m = \kappa^{(y)}_m x^m$ does not increase on $m \ge 1$.

Parking.zrT — The tilted environment $z^{(y)}_N x^N$ of a threshold $y$ at a tilt $x$, where $z^{(y)}_N = A(N,y-1)/N!$ is the normalised number of parking functions of length $N$ with all displacements smaller than $y$.
Parking.zrT_succ — For a threshold $y \ge 1$ and a tilt $x$, the tilted environment $u_N = z^{(y)}_N x^N$ satisfies $(N+1)\,u_{N+1} = x \sum_{i=0}^{N} \min(i+1,y)\, u_i\, u_{N-i}$.

Parking.cayleySum_le_one — For $k \ge 12$ the Cayley sum at the critical tilt is at most one: $x_k \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j x_k^j \le 1$, where $c_j = (j+1)^{j-1}/j!$ and $x_k = (k/(k+1))^{k-1}$. Equivalently $\sum_{n=2}^{k+1} a_n x_k^n \le 1$ for the tree numbers $a_n = n^{n-1}/n!$.
g.text: the Cayley sum at the critical

g.title: Parking.ccT_le_succ — At the critical tilt $x_k$, $k \ge 1$, the tilted Cayley masses do not decrease from the index $k-1$ on: $c_n x_k^n \le c_{n+1} x_k^{n+1}$ whenever $n + 1 \ge k$.
Parking.ccT_succ_le — At the critical tilt $x_k$ the tilted Cayley masses do not increase up to the index $k$: $c_{n+1} x_k^{n+1} \le c_n x_k^n$ whenever $n + 1 \le k$.
g.text: not increase up to the critical

g.title: Parking.epsT_succ_le — At the critical tilt $x_k$ the tilted free prime kernel does not increase on $1 \le m \le k$: $\varepsilon_{m+1} x_k^{m+1} \le \varepsilon_m x_k^m$ for $1 \le m < k$.
g.text: does not increase up to the

g.title: Parking.xcrit — The critical tilt $x_k = (k/(k+1))^{k-1}$ of the column $k$: the tilt at which the tilted Cayley masses $c_n x^n$ of the indices $k-1$ and $k$ are equal.
Parking.xcrit_mul_psi — For $k \ge 1$ the critical tilt satisfies $x_k\,(1 + 1/k)^{k-1} = 1$.

Parking.zrT_anti_crit — For every column $k \ge 2$ the tilted environment of the threshold $k$ at the critical tilt, $z^{(k)}_N x_k^N$ with $z^{(k)}_N = A(N,k-1)/N!$ and $x_k = (k/(k+1))^{k-1}$, is nonincreasing in $N$.
g.text: not increase at the critical tilt

g.title: Parking.no_descent_ascent — No row of the numbers $b(n,\ell)$ has a strict descent followed by a strict ascent: there are no $1\le i<j\le n-1$ with $b(n,i)<b(n,i-1)$ and $b(n,j-1)<b(n,j)$.

Parking.right_tail — To the right of the middle of a row, a nonpositive step is followed only by nonpositive steps: if $i\ge9$, $n\le2i-1$ and $b(n,i)\le b(n,i-1)$, then $b(m,j)\le b(m,j-1)$ for every column $j\ge i$ and every row $m$ with $j+1\le m\le n$.

Parking.unimodal_of_no_pair — A finite sequence of natural numbers that has no strict descent followed, at a later position, by a strict ascent is unimodal: it is nondecreasing up to some position and nonincreasing from that position on.
